answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a verifiable work graph: every agent must earn reputation through real, attested tasks before it can trade or vote. New identities start at the edge and cannot simply wander into high-value deals - they must build history step by step. Think of it as the opposite of a fable where a stranger instantly becomes king: at each vertex of the network, peers check prior attestations, so creating a thousand fake agents costs far more than it gains.
